name: Overhead Core
description: The settings and the paintings page for the Overhead widgets (overhead_photo, overhead_plate, overhead_cluster, overhead_scene): the fal.ai key, the daily limits, the contact for planespotters.net and the logo service. No widget of its own.

settings.name: fal_api_key
settings.label: fal.ai API key (AI paintings)
settings.help: With a key the widgets can paint each aircraft from its own photograph, at about US$0.04 a painting, once per airframe and style. Get one at https://fal.ai/dashboard/keys; it is only sent to fal.run. Without one the widgets show photographs.

settings.name: contact
settings.label: Contact for planespotters.net
settings.help: An email address or a web page, sent in the widget's User-Agent as planespotters.net asks of every application. The widget names its own project page by default; give your own contact if their API starts refusing the lookups (the widgets then show silhouettes).

settings.name: gen_daily_usd
settings.label: Painting budget per day
settings.help: The most the widgets may spend on new paintings in a day, at the models' listed prices (US$4 is about a hundred Nano Banana paintings). 0 is no limit. Paintings are kept, so an airframe in a style only costs once; after a few weeks most of what passes is already painted.

settings.name: gen_per_refresh
settings.label: New paintings started per preview
settings.help: How many new paintings one settled preview in the editor may start (1 to 50). A panel's own render starts what its page needs, within the daily number.

settings.name: gen_parallel
settings.label: Paintings made at once
settings.help: How many paintings fal.ai works on side by side (1 to 8).

settings.name: logo_source
settings.label: Airline logos from
settings.help: Where a widget with Airline logos on fetches them, at render time; nothing is stored with the widget. Daisycon serves wide wordmarks, Kiwi square icons. Both are third-party services that may change; the airline's name is shown when a logo is missing.

settings.name: visitor_refs
settings.label: Your own reference pictures for the visitors
settings.help: One a line, craft = picture: for example nostromo = https://example.org/nostromo.jpg or viper = /home/pi/pictures/viper.png. The craft's id is the word before the colon in the Who visits list (saucer, triangle, cigar, orb, tictac, adamski, enterprise, falcon, xwing, tie, destroyer, nostromo, serenity, discovery, eagle, tb2, birdofprey, rocinante, viper, tardis, heartofgold, shuttle, apollo_csm, lunar_module, sputnik, starship, vostok, voyager, iss, zeppelin). Yours is used over the bundled one. The picture is fetched or read by this server and sent to fal.ai for the craft's shape; what you may use is your own call.
